fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Aquarian Energy and the Rise of Inner Technology", "body": "Chance opens Gemini season asking how astrological awareness moves from hindsight to foresight, and Ashley Mosaic corrects his first guess: she is a Capricorn with her moon in Aquarius, a placement she says shows up in every facet of her life. Mosaic describes Aquarian energy as expansion, evolution of consciousness and technology at once, arguing that as human consciousness expands, technology accelerates in tandem, and that our job is balancing the two. Chance pushes back toward the older meaning of technology, which once referred to language and the terms of art of a craft, making our inner dialogue a kind of inner technology."}, {"title": "Astrology as the Weatherman's First Glance", "body": "Asked whether the stars influence us or reflect us, Mosaic refuses to pick, offering three readings she holds at once: direct planetary influence, epigenetic imprints stamped at birth, and archetypes simply playing out through everyone. She says she wants the rationality and does not know why it works, only that it does. Her working analogy is meteorology: astrology is stepping outside and seeing the sky is gray and full of storm clouds, after which she reaches for her other tools, other cycles and other charts. Chance answers that he keeps multiple models running because nothing finite can model something as infinite as the universe."}, {"title": "The 2020 Forecast She Made in 2018", "body": "Mosaic recounts telling people in 2018 that something world changing was coming in 2020. Her stated evidence was a Pluto and Saturn conjunction in Capricorn, a sign she reads as authority, big business and government, with a south node conjunction added in, a pairing she says had not occurred there since the 1500s. She points to Jupiter crossing that exact degree on March 17th, when COVID news broke and everything closed, and to Saturn entering Aquarius as restrictions loosened, then retrograding as masks returned. She also notes Pluto was crossing her own sun, which made the period personally intense."}, {"title": "Human Design as the Compass to Astrology's Map", "body": "Mosaic defines human design as our mechanics, built on top of astrology and personalized into the body, so that you no longer just have the map but a compass to walk through it, an analogy Chance says works for him. She frames it against what she calls mass homogenization, where everyone tries to be one figure doing things one way, leaving people fragmented and unsure whose life they are living. She cites her own sun in gate 61, universal laws and dot connecting, ties the 64 I Ching hexagrams to the 64 gates and gene keys, and predicts human design will land where Enneagram and Myers-Briggs were a decade ago."}, {"title": "Two Marses, Company Charts and the Moving Goalposts", "body": "Mosaic walks Chance through the design and personality columns, calling the design side our self-driving Tesla, encoded roughly 88 days before birth. Reading his design Mars in gate 51, the arousing and the gate of shock, she argues agitation is meant to trigger initiation rather than be absorbed Eeyore style, and reads his personality Mars in 16, enthusiasm and magical genius, whose shadow is indifference. In consulting she charts five or six leaders, seats idea curators apart from builders, and says color returns to their faces. Chance closes with biofield work, warning that hanging self-acceptance on a future goal only moves the goalposts."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The futurist & guide to Human Design, Ashley Mosaic, joins InnerVerse to discuss the insights she's gained from astrological foresight. We discuss how the transits of 2020 helped her see and prepare for what was coming for the world, and the most effective ways to benefit from paying attention to the sky clock, how Human Design is the compass to the map of your stars, the role of Mars in HD and other aspects of the body chart, and how Ashley helps clients by fusing HD with analytical foresight to make them more effective in their livelihoods.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension, we consider what it means to be a futurist, the forecast for 2027 to 2030, an honest look at what's probably coming down the pike with blockchain and crypto, the energetic keys to financially thriving, where self-worth and abundance intersect in the Biofield, the aesthetics of success, the philosophy of getting started, and using ChatGPT to deep dive your own life story.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Futurism as a Way of Thinking", "body": "Ashley defines a futurist as simply someone future oriented, someone who reads patterns and carries the energetics and self-concept to act on what the foresight shows. Asked what few people are discussing, she offers her own reading of the sky clock: favorable Neptune aspects that she likens to rose colored glasses, followed around 2029 and 2030 by cycles she compares to the World War II era, when she suspects the glasses come off. She treats 2027 as a turn from tribal bargaining toward individual responsibility and urges listeners to find their single points of failure. Both agree nobody is worse off for knowing how to grow food."}, {"title": "Blockchain, Power and Healthy Skepticism", "body": "Ashley recalls first hearing about Bitcoin in 2012 and grasping its promise of autonomy and transparency, yet she frames the technology as neutral and the real contest as one of power, noting that big banks called it a scam while building their own systems. Chance, a former IT guy, voices healthy skepticism about complexity held together with duct tape and a crypto casino that ends up favoring the big players. Ashley, who has worked with blockchain projects, admits true decentralization means no decision maker and a constant meeting of the minds. She now sees several possible timelines rather than one, and her takeaway is personal: be scrappier."}, {"title": "Self Concept, Shame and Money Patterns", "body": "Ashley argues that foresight alone does not build security, because in her experience energetics and concept of self have to be in alignment first. She describes get money, lose it cycles, a nervous system addicted to struggle, and the temptation to blame larger systems. Chance adds a tuning example where a snag in a client's paternal ancestral river pointed to poverty consciousness, where living only for needs left wants out of the picture. Ashley maps this onto the root chakra, which may attract but never keep, and the sacral, where desire and shame live, recalling how gratitude for any audience led her to underprice her readings and burn out."}, {"title": "Burnout, Pricing and Energy Types", "body": "Chance reports that many people he tunes hold tension in the hips tied to an unconscious value placed on burnout, and he says the body obliges by cutting sleep short. His remedy is a pricing model built around the whole healthy lifestyle a practitioner needs rather than the single hour or product, hence his limit of one or two sessions a day. Ashley carries the point into human design: an undefined root center makes burnout more likely, projectors without a defined sacral are here to guide rather than work all day, and a manifesting generator like Chance is built to move fast, skip steps and keep several projects going."}, {"title": "Aesthetics, Starting and Owning Your Story", "body": "Asked whether aesthetics matter for success, Ashley answers that reality is created in the mind, so looks matter as much as you believe they do, and she warns that perfection is not real. Chance counters with the philosophical case for beauty, pointing to ornate antiques and to mundus and cosmos as words for order that adorns. On getting started, Ashley says the road to purpose is paved with your pain, so solve your own problem, then help others solve it. She closes by urging a deep dive on your life story, because your weird is your superpower, and Chance ties weird to the old word wyrd, meaning fate or destiny."}]
